purpose: The corrected LSG pool. Replaces the frozen 12-species genEra panel's 842 HAP1 / 883 HAP2 with 776 / 835, and carries BOTH ranks per gene so the atlas can show the correction rather than silently swap one number for another.
status_2026_09_26: THE POOL AGAIN (ms2-lsg docs/CORRECTIONS.md C5, commit 8eb65b0; Chen, 2026-09-21 evening, reconfirmed 2026-09-26): rank >= 18 in this table is the LSG pool, 776 HAP1 + 835 HAP2 (PS18/PS19 433/343 and 497/338). Applied by scripts/patch_lsg_pool.py: ps.* is this table's call, and the frozen call sits under ps.frz wherever its rank differs (766 genes). The status_2026_09_21 line below describes the arrangement of 2026-09-21 to 09-26 (C4) and is kept as written.
status_2026_09_21: SUPERSEDED AS THE POOL. Chen ruled on 2026-09-21 that the LSG pool is the frozen genEra call, 842 HAP1 + 883 HAP2, and does not change; every check on it, this rerun included, is a per-gene flag (MS2_2026 CLAUDE.md, commit 1e698f2). This table is now the source of the per-gene rerun call (ps.rr, where its rank differs) and of the flag qc.rr (a pool gene that falls below rank 18 here: 66 HAP1 + 48 HAP2). The pool itself comes from sources/lsg_pool_frozen.tsv.gz. The rerun was also the first run to search the full comparison panel (the frozen call searched NCBI nr only), so a rank change here is not always due to Idesia. The text below is kept as written on 2026-09-10.
why_public: Derived from published genome assemblies and genEra, a public method. docs/EMBARGO.md's 'Not affected' list names phylostratigraphy and the genEra layer as publishable. The atlas already publishes the frozen ranks; this corrects them.

adoption.supersedes: sources/lsg_qc_flags.provenance.json's `idesia_deliberately_excluded` block, which said 'Chen has not adopted it'. That was true when written on 2026-09-06 and is not true now.

scope: genome-wide, every gene in the atlas -- not just the pool. Ranks moved for 766 genes, of which the pool boundary accounts for a minority.
join_key: gene_id, bare locus, matches the atlas gene index
why_the_pool_moved: Idesia polycarpa is the only available Salicaceae genome outside Saliceae and was never in the 12-species panel. That is a sampling gap exactly where an LSG call is made: a gene present in Populus and Idesia but lost in Salix reads as Populus-specific. Adding it removes 66 HAP1 and 48 HAP2 genes and adds NONE. One-directional movement is the signature of adding real homology signal; a noisy rerun would move genes both ways. Reproduced identically across two passes.
the_part_that_is_more_than_a_headcount: 179 genes move PS19 -> PS18 and STAY in the pool; none move the other way. Pool composition goes from 51.0% PS19 / 49.0% PS18 to 42.3% / 57.7%. The atlas labels PS19 'hybrid-only', so before this correction the site showed a stratum name the source no longer assigns to a fifth of that arm. PS18 and PS19 are never pooled by upstream policy and must not be pooled here.
what_adoption_does_NOT_license: abSENSE corrects homology-detection FAILURE, a sensitivity problem. A missing genome is taxon SAMPLING, a coverage problem. Both surface identically as 'no homolog found' and only the first is fixable by modelling: 86% of the genes Idesia removed were `no_prediction` in the frozen abSENSE run, i.e. abSENSE could say nothing about them at all. The corrected pool is NOT evidence that the surviving calls are modelled-safe. See sources/lsg_qc_flags.provenance.json and the calibration note in data/meta/manifest.json.

columns_dropped_before_shipping.why: They carry the unpublished LSG candidate names for 10 genes (the names themselves are withheld here since 2026-09-21: this record is rendered on the public site). TODO 22's hold on candidate labels is unchanged by C2's adoption; the pool moving does not release the names. patch_lsg_pool.py (then patch_pool_idesia.py) asserts both are absent from this file before reading a row, the same construction patch_lsg_qc.py uses.

columns.rank, phylostratum, tax_rep, age_class,: the rerun's call, with Idesia added and the full comparison panel searched. Canonical as the pool until 2026-09-21; since then shown per gene as ps.rr and used as the qc.rr flag.
columns.frozen_rank, frozen_is_lsg: the frozen genEra call. C2 withdrew it as the CANONICAL pool, but it is still the pool the chapter text reports (842/883, named as frozen, with 776/835 alongside as the robustness check; Chen, 2026-09-20). Kept so a reader can see what changed and so numbers published against the frozen pool remain checkable -- they are correct statements about that pool and are not retracted. (2026-09-21: an MS2 consistency audit, A38, found the frozen run searched nr only rather than a 12-species panel, so this line no longer calls it a panel call; the other lines of this record keep C2's wording until Chen rules.)
columns.left_pool_under_idesia: was rank >= 18 on the frozen panel, is not now. 66 HAP1 + 48 HAP2.
columns.entered_pool_under_idesia: would be the reverse. It is zero for every gene, by construction, and the patcher asserts that.

gate_run_before_adoption: Every one of the 63,960 genes' `frozen_rank` was checked against the rank the atlas was already serving. Zero mismatches, and no gene present in one and absent from the other. That is what makes this a one-step auditable correction rather than a re-derivation: the source's frozen column IS the layer the atlas shipped. patch_lsg_pool.py (then patch_pool_idesia.py) re-runs that gate on every build and refuses to write if it ever fails.
